items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the travel prose 'Glimpses of India', and answer.

"Every morning, before the cocks had finished crowing, the bread-seller cycled into our lane. A bell on his handlebar rang twice, and doors opened all along the street. Children ran out in their nightclothes to choose the softest buns, while mothers argued cheerfully about the price. Years later, in a city flat, I still wake at that hour listening for the bell that no longer comes."
